es.B: El oráculo que vio el profeta Habacuc.

fr.L: L’oracle que vit Habacuc le prophète.
fr.B: L’oracle que le prophète Habacuc vit.

sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao nabii Habakuki aliupokea katika maono.

vi.L: Sấm ngôn mà Ha-ba-cúc, nhà tiên tri, đã thấy.
vi.B: Sấm ngôn mà nhà tiên tri Ha-ba-cúc đã thấy.

ko.R: 이것은 예언자 하박국이 환상 가운데 받은 말씀이다.

decisions.choice: oracle: a solemn pronouncement from God
decisions.reason: The word heads prophetic messages, especially messages of judgment (Isaiah 13:1; Nahum 1:1; Malachi 1:1). Here it introduces a book that begins with the prophet's own complaint to God, God's answer and a prayer; the whole is the message God gave him (see the note at Isaiah 13:1).

decisions.choice: Habakkuk the prophet: a prophet in the last years of Judah
decisions.reason: Nothing is known of Habakkuk beyond this book; the meaning of his name is uncertain. The book speaks of the Chaldeans, the Babylonians, as about to rise to power (1:6). That points to the last decades before Babylon took Jerusalem, around the time Nebuchadnezzar defeated Egypt at Carchemish (605 BC). Habakkuk is one of the few prophets called "the prophet" in the heading of his book, as Haggai and Zechariah are.

decisions.choice: saw: received in a vision
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for a prophet's vision (Isaiah 1:1; Amos 1:1). What the prophet "saw" was a message from God, and God tells him to write "the vision" in 2:2.

decisions.choice: message; received in a vision
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and Nahum, Readable says "message" for "oracle" and explains "saw".

decisions.choice: "El oráculo" (L, B); "el mensaje" (R) for *massa*, as the prophets' headings; "recibió en una visión" (R) for "saw"
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *massa* in the prophets; Readable explains the vision as the English does.

decisions.choice: "L'oracle" (L, B); "le message" (R), for *massa*, in Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai and Zechariah
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for *massa* as a title ("Oracle sur …" / "Message au sujet de …"), here without a named nation; Readable says what the English Readable says, a message received in a vision.

decisions.choice: The prophets' words, complaints and God's answers are speech: present, future and passé composé at every level, never passé simple; the past in Habakkuk 3 is in the passé composé, as the Psalms. Narrative frames (Haggai's dated reports, Zechariah's visions told in the first person) take the passé simple at L and B and the passé composé at R
alternatives: passé simple for past events at L and B throughout
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for Lamentations, Ezekiel, Daniel and the Twelve: oracles and prayers are spoken, not written narration. The heading keeps "vit" at L and B, as Isaiah 13:1.

decisions.choice: "Unabii" (L, B); "ujumbe" (R) for *massa*; "nabii Habakuki"
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *massa* in the prophets (Isaiah); Readable says the message came in a vision, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Sấm ngôn" (L, B); "sứ điệp" (R) for *massa*; "nhà tiên tri Ha-ba-cúc"
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *massa* (Nahum 1:1; Isaiah); Readable explains "saw" as receiving the message in a vision.

decisions.choice: "신탁" (L, B); "말씀" (R) for *massa*; "예언자 하박국"
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *massa* in the prophets; Readable says he received the word in a vision, as the English does.

source.text: עַד־אָ֧נָה יְהוָ֛ה שִׁוַּ֖עְתִּי וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁמָ֑ע אֶזְעַ֥ק אֵלֶ֛יךָ חָמָ֖ס וְלֹ֥א תוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Until when, Yahweh, have I cried for help, and you do not hear? I cry out to you, Violence! and you do not save.

en.L: How long, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have I cried for help, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not hear? \q I cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, "Violence!" and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not save.
en.B: How long, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, must I cry for help while {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not listen? \q I cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, "Violence!" but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not save.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, how long must I call to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} listen? \q I cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that violence is everywhere, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not rescue us.

es.L: ¿Hasta cuándo, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, he clamado por auxilio, y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} no oyes? \q Clamo a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}: «¡Violencia!», y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} no salvas.
es.B: ¿Hasta cuándo, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, tendré que pedir auxilio sin que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} escuches? \q Clamo a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}: «¡Violencia!», pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} no salvas.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¿cuánto tiempo más tendré que clamar a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} pidiendo ayuda antes de que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me escuches? \q Clamo a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} que hay violencia por todas partes, pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} no nos rescatas.

fr.L: Jusqu’à quand, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ai-je crié au secours, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} n’entends pas ? \q Je crie vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} : « Violence ! » et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne sauves pas.
fr.B: Jusqu’à quand, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, devrai-je appeler au secours sans que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} écoutes ? \q Je crie vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} : « Violence ! » mais {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne sauves pas.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, combien de temps vais-je encore {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} supplier de m’aider avant que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’écoutes ? \q Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} crie que la violence est partout, mais {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne nous délivres pas.

sw.L: Hadi lini, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nimelia kuomba msaada, {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} husikii? \q Nakulilia, "Ukatili!" {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} huokoi.
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitaomba msaada hadi lini, {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} husikilizi? \q Nakulilia, "Ukatili!" lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} huokoi.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakulilia hadi lini ili unisaidie, kabla hujanisikiliza? \q Nakulilia kwamba ukatili uko kila mahali, lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} hutuokoi.

vi.L: Cho đến bao giờ, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, con đã kêu cứu mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không nghe? \q Con kêu lên với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Bạo lực!" mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không giải cứu.
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, con phải kêu cứu đến bao giờ mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vẫn không lắng nghe? \q Con kêu lên với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Bạo lực!" nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không cứu.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, con phải kêu xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giúp đỡ đến bao giờ thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mới nghe? \q Con kêu với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rằng bạo lực ở khắp nơi, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không giải cứu chúng con.

ko.L: 언제까지입니까, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여? 제가 도와 달라고 부르짖었는데 주님께서는 듣지 않으십니다. \q 제가 주님께 "폭력이다!" 하고 외쳐도 주님께서는 구원하지 않으십니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 들어 주지 않으시는데 제가 언제까지 도와 달라고 부르짖어야 합니까? \q 제가 주님께 "폭력이다!" 하고 외쳐도 주님께서는 구원하지 않으십니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 들어 주실 때까지 제가 언제까지 도와 달라고 외쳐야 합니까? \q 곳곳에 폭력이 판친다고 주님께 부르짖어도 주님께서는 저희를 구해 주지 않으십니다.

decisions.choice: How long, LORD?: the prophet's complaint to God
decisions.reason: The book opens not with God's word to the people but with the prophet's words to God. "How long?" is the cry of the lament psalms (Psalm 13:2-3; 74:10). Habakkuk complains in 1:2-4, the LORD answers in 1:5-11, Habakkuk complains again in 1:12-2:1, and the LORD answers in 2:2-20.

decisions.choice: Violence!: the cry of someone being wronged
decisions.reason: The word means violent wrongdoing: brutality, oppression, the crushing of the weak (Genesis 6:11; Jeremiah 6:7). Crying "Violence!" was a call for help, like crying "Help!" or "Murder!" (Job 19:7; Jeremiah 20:8). Verses 3-4 show that the violence is within Judah itself.

decisions.choice: that violence is everywhere; rescue us
decisions.reason: Readable makes the cry part of the sentence and adds "us", the people who suffer the violence.

decisions.choice: Every YHWH is a divine_name span, "el SEÑOR" by default with "Yahvé" as the alternative; the vocative is "{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}" with no "oh". Habakkuk speaks to God with "tú", and God's free pronouns take deity_pronoun spans ("{{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}", "{{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}")
decisions.reason: The settled forms for the prophets and the Psalms; the book opens with the prophet's own complaint to God (m1).

decisions.choice: "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}" for the vocative (L, B), plain at R; deity_pronoun spans go only on free pronouns ("nawe", "wewe"), never on verb prefixes
decisions.reason: The settled vocative of the Psalms and prophets; Swahili marks God's "you" mostly in the verb, which takes no span.

decisions.choice: "Ukatili!" for the cry *chamas*
decisions.reason: The cry names brutal wrongdoing (m2); "ukatili" is the common word for violence and cruelty, and the same word is used through the book.

decisions.choice: Every YHWH is {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Habakkuk calls himself "con" and God "Ngài" (spanned mid-sentence), with "lạy CHÚA" and no "O"; he speaks for the people as "chúng con"
decisions.reason: The settled address of a prophet praying to God (Jonah 4:2; the Isaiah note).

decisions.choice: Every YHWH is {{divine_name:주|야훼}}. Habakkuk speaks to God in 합쇼체 with "저" ("저희" for the people), calling him "주님" and "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여"; God answers in 해라체 (1:5-11; 2:2-20)
decisions.reason: The settled speech levels: prayer is 합쇼체, and God speaks in the plain 해라체 without -시-.

source.text: לָ֣מָּה תַרְאֵ֤נִי אָ֨וֶן֙ וְעָמָ֣ל תַּבִּ֔יט וְשֹׁ֥ד וְחָמָ֖ס לְנֶגְדִּ֑י וַיְהִ֧י רִ֦יב וּמָד֖וֹן יִשָּֽׂא׃

records.literal_gloss: Why do you make me see iniquity, and trouble do you look at? And destruction and violence [are] before me; and there is strife, and contention arises.

en.L: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make me see iniquity, and [why] do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} look on trouble? \q Destruction and violence [are] before me; \q there is strife, and contention arises.
en.B: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make me see wrongdoing? Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put up with trouble? \q Ruin and violence are in front of me; \q quarrels and conflict break out.
en.R: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make me watch people do evil? Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} just look on while they cause trouble? \q Everywhere I look there is destruction and violence. \q People argue and fight.

es.L: ¿Por qué me haces ver la iniquidad, y [por qué] miras {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} la aflicción? \q Destrucción y violencia [están] delante de mí; \q hay contienda, y se levanta la discordia.
es.B: ¿Por qué me haces ver el mal? ¿Por qué toleras la opresión? \q Tengo ante mis ojos ruina y violencia; \q estallan pleitos y conflictos.
es.R: ¿Por qué me haces ver cómo la gente hace el mal? ¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} solo miras mientras causan sufrimiento? \q Dondequiera que miro hay destrucción y violencia. \q La gente discute y pelea.

fr.L: Pourquoi me fais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} voir l’iniquité, et [pourquoi] regardes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} la peine ? \q Dévastation et violence [sont] devant moi ; \q il y a querelle, et la discorde s’élève.
fr.B: Pourquoi me fais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} voir le mal ? Pourquoi tolères-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} la misère ? \q Le ravage et la violence sont sous mes yeux ; \q les querelles et les conflits éclatent.
fr.R: Pourquoi me fais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} voir des gens faire le mal ? Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} contentes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} de regarder pendant qu’ils causent du malheur ? \q Partout où je regarde, il y a destruction et violence. \q Les gens se disputent et se battent.

sw.L: Kwa nini unanionyesha uovu, na [kwa nini] unaitazama taabu? \q Uharibifu na ukatili [viko] mbele yangu; \q kuna ugomvi, na mashindano yanainuka.
sw.B: Kwa nini unanifanya nione maovu? Kwa nini unavumilia taabu? \q Uharibifu na ukatili viko mbele ya macho yangu; \q ugomvi na mapambano yanazuka.
sw.R: Kwa nini unanifanya nitazame watu wakitenda maovu? Kwa nini unatazama tu wanaposababisha taabu? \q Kila ninapotazama kuna uharibifu na ukatili. \q Watu wanabishana na kupigana.

vi.L: Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt con thấy điều gian ác, và [sao] {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhìn xem điều khổ nạn? \q Sự tàn phá và bạo lực [ở] trước mặt con; \q có tranh chấp, và xung đột nổi lên.
vi.B: Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt con thấy điều sai trái? Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dung thứ cảnh khổ ải? \q Sự hủy hoại và bạo lực ở ngay trước mắt con; \q cãi cọ và xung đột bùng lên.
vi.R: Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt con phải nhìn người ta làm điều ác? Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cứ đứng nhìn trong khi họ gây khổ cho người khác? \q Con nhìn đâu cũng thấy tàn phá và bạo lực. \q Người ta cãi nhau và đánh nhau.

ko.L: 어찌하여 주님께서는 제게 죄악을 보게 하시며, [어찌하여] 고난을 바라보십니까? \q 파멸과 폭력이 제 앞에 [있고], \q 다툼이 있고 분쟁이 일어납니다.
ko.B: 어찌하여 주님께서는 제게 악을 보게 하십니까? 어찌하여 고통을 그대로 두십니까? \q 파괴와 폭력이 제 눈앞에 있고, \q 싸움과 다툼이 끊이지 않습니다.
ko.R: 어찌하여 주님께서는 사람들이 악한 일을 하는 것을 제게 보게 하십니까? 그들이 괴로움을 끼치는데 어찌하여 그저 보고만 계십니까? \q 어디를 보아도 파괴와 폭력뿐입니다. \q 사람들이 말다툼하고 싸웁니다.

decisions.choice: iniquity and trouble: wickedness and the misery it causes
decisions.reason: The first word is wrongdoing, especially deceit and the abuse of power; the second is the trouble and suffering it brings on others. They are often paired (Psalm 10:7; Isaiah 10:1; Job 4:8).

decisions.choice: do you look on trouble?: God seems to watch and do nothing
alternatives: why do you make me look at trouble?
decisions.reason: The verb may mean "you look on" or "you make me look". The same verb is used of God in verse 13 ("why do you look on the treacherous?"), so it is taken here of God looking on without acting.

decisions.choice: strife and contention: quarrels and lawsuits
decisions.reason: The two words are used of quarrels and of disputes in court. They lead into verse 4, where the courts fail.

decisions.choice: put up with (B); just look on while (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what it means for God to "look on" trouble without stopping it (m2).

source.text: עַל־כֵּן֙ תָּפ֣וּג תּוֹרָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־יֵצֵ֥א לָנֶ֖צַח מִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּ֤י רָשָׁע֙ מַכְתִּ֣יר אֶת־הַצַּדִּ֔יק עַל־כֵּ֛ן יֵצֵ֥א מִשְׁפָּ֖ט מְעֻקָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore grows numb [the] instruction, and not goes forth to perpetuity justice; for [the] wicked surrounds the righteous; therefore justice goes forth perverted.

en.L: Therefore [the] instruction grows numb, \q and justice never goes forth; \q for [the] wicked surround the righteous; \q therefore justice goes forth twisted.
en.B: So the instruction loses its force, \q and justice never wins out. \q The wicked hem in the righteous, \q so justice comes out twisted.
en.R: That is why God's teaching has no power, \q and justice never wins. \q Wicked people surround those who do right, \q so justice is twisted.

es.L: Por eso se entorpece la instrucción, \q y nunca sale el derecho; \q porque el malvado cerca al justo; \q por eso sale torcido el derecho.
es.B: Por eso la instrucción pierde su fuerza, \q y el derecho nunca prevalece. \q Los malvados acorralan a los justos, \q y así el derecho sale torcido.
es.R: Por eso la enseñanza de Dios no tiene poder, \q y la justicia nunca gana. \q Los malvados rodean a los que hacen lo correcto, \q así que la justicia queda torcida.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi la loi s’engourdit, \q et le droit ne sort jamais ; \q car le méchant encercle le juste ; \q c’est pourquoi le droit sort tordu.
fr.B: Aussi l’instruction perd-elle sa force, \q et le droit ne triomphe jamais. \q Les méchants encerclent les justes, \q et le droit en sort faussé.
fr.R: Voilà pourquoi l’enseignement de Dieu n’a plus de force, \q et la justice ne gagne jamais. \q Les méchants entourent ceux qui font ce qui est juste, \q alors la justice est faussée.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo sheria inalegea, \q wala hukumu haitoki kamwe; \q kwa maana mwovu anamzunguka mwenye haki; \q kwa hiyo hukumu inatoka ikiwa imepotoka.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo mafundisho yanapoteza nguvu, \q na haki haishindi kamwe. \q Waovu wanawazingira wenye haki, \q kwa hiyo haki inatoka ikiwa imepindishwa.
sw.R: Ndiyo maana mafundisho ya Mungu hayana nguvu, \q na haki haishindi kamwe. \q Watu waovu wanawazunguka wale wanaotenda haki, \q kwa hiyo haki inapotoshwa.

vi.L: Vì vậy luật pháp tê liệt, \q và công lý chẳng bao giờ ra; \q vì kẻ ác vây quanh người công chính; \q vì vậy công lý ra cong vẹo.
vi.B: Vì thế lời dạy dỗ mất hết sức mạnh, \q và công lý chẳng bao giờ thắng. \q Kẻ ác vây hãm người công chính, \q nên công lý bị bẻ cong.
vi.R: Vì thế lời dạy của Đức Chúa Trời không còn sức mạnh, \q và công lý không bao giờ thắng. \q Kẻ ác vây quanh những người làm điều ngay thẳng, \q nên công lý bị bẻ cong.

ko.L: 그러므로 가르침이 힘을 잃고, \q 정의가 결코 나오지 않습니다. \q 악인이 의인을 에워싸니, \q 그러므로 정의가 굽게 나옵니다.
ko.B: 그래서 가르침은 힘을 잃고, \q 정의는 끝내 이기지 못합니다. \q 악인들이 의인들을 에워싸니, \q 정의가 굽어져 나옵니다.
ko.R: 그래서 하나님의 가르침이 힘을 잃었고, \q 정의는 결코 이기지 못합니다. \q 악한 사람들이 바르게 사는 사람들을 둘러싸고 있으니, \q 정의가 비뚤어집니다.

decisions.choice: instruction: God's teaching, as the rule of life and of the courts
decisions.reason: The word (*torah*) is God's instruction to his people: the teaching of the covenant, applied by priests and judges in settling disputes (Deuteronomy 17:8-11). When it "grows numb" it has lost its force: it no longer restrains anyone.

decisions.choice: grows numb ... justice never goes forth
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow numb or cold, to lose feeling and strength (Genesis 45:26; Psalm 77:3). The phrase "never goes forth" may also be read "never goes forth victorious": justice never comes out the winner.

decisions.choice: the wicked and the righteous: Habakkuk's complaint is about Judah
alternatives: the wicked are a foreign oppressor
decisions.reason: The wicked who surround the righteous are most likely the powerful in Judah who bend the courts against honest people, as in the complaints of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 5:26-28) and Amos (5:12). The LORD's answer, that he is sending the Chaldeans (verses 5-11), is his judgment on this injustice. Some take the wicked to be a foreign oppressor already here.

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B); God's teaching (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *torah* in the prophets: "instruction" at Literal and Balanced, "teaching" at Readable, which adds "God's" to say whose teaching it is.

decisions.choice: *torah* "la instrucción" (L, B), "la enseñanza de Dios" (R); *mishpat* "el derecho" (L, B), "la justicia" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled words of the prophets (Isaiah, Psalms); Readable says "la justicia" where the English Readable keeps "justice".

decisions.choice: *torah* "la loi" (L), "l'instruction" (B), "l'enseignement de Dieu" (R); *mishpat* "le droit" (L, B), "la justice" (R)
decisions.reason: As the prophets in French: God's *torah* is "loi" / "instruction" / "enseignement", lowercase, since it is God's teaching in general, not the named Law of Moses; *mishpat* is "le droit" at L and B, as Isaiah, and plain "la justice" at R.

decisions.choice: *torah* "sheria" (L), "mafundisho" (B), "mafundisho ya Mungu" (R); *mishpat* "hukumu" (L), "haki" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled words for God's instruction and for justice in the prophets (Isaiah 28:17).

decisions.choice: *torah* "luật pháp" (L), "lời dạy dỗ" (B), "lời dạy của Đức Chúa Trời" (R), as Isaiah 2:3; "tê liệt" (L) for "grows numb"
decisions.reason: The published words for God's instruction at each level; the verb keeps the picture of numbness at Literal (m2).

decisions.choice: "가르침" for *torah* at every level (R "하나님의 가르침"); the complaint stays 합쇼체 because Habakkuk is still speaking to God
decisions.reason: As Isaiah 2:3; 율법 is kept for the Law in the New Testament.

source.text: רְא֤וּ בַגּוֹיִם֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטוּ וְהִֽתַּמְּה֖וּ תְּמָ֑הוּ כִּי־פֹ֨עַל֙ פֹּעֵ֣ל בִּֽימֵיכֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תַאֲמִ֖ינוּ כִּ֥י יְסֻפָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: See among [the] nations and look, and be astonished, be astounded; for a deed [I am] doing in your days; not you will believe if it is told.

en.L: Look among the nations, and watch, \q and be astonished, be astounded! \q For a work [I am] working in your days \q [that] you would not believe if it were told.
en.B: Look at the nations and watch, \q and be utterly astonished! \q For I am doing something in your days \q that you would not believe even if you were told.
en.R: Look at what is happening among the nations! \q Be amazed and astonished! \q I am about to do something in your lifetime \q that you would not believe even if someone told you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} entre las naciones, y {{plural_you:observen|observad}}, \q ¡y {{plural_you:asómbrense|asombraos}}, {{plural_you:quédense pasmados|quedaos pasmados}}! \q Porque [yo] hago una obra en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} días \q [que] no {{plural_you:creerían|creeríais}} si fuera contada.
es.B: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} entre las naciones y {{plural_you:observen|observad}}, \q ¡{{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} completamente asombrados! \q Porque yo hago una obra en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} días \q que no {{plural_you:creerían|creeríais}} aunque alguien {{plural_you:se la contara|os la contara}}.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} lo que sucede entre las naciones! \q ¡{{plural_you:Asómbrense|Asombraos}} y {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} con la boca abierta! \q Durante {{plural_you:su vida|vuestra vida}} voy a hacer algo \q que no {{plural_you:creerían|creeríais}} aunque alguien {{plural_you:se lo contara|os lo contara}}.

fr.L: Regardez parmi les nations, et observez, \q et soyez étonnés, soyez stupéfaits ! \q Car [je] fais une œuvre en vos jours, \q vous ne [la] croiriez pas si elle était racontée.
fr.B: Regardez les nations et observez, \q soyez saisis de stupeur ! \q Car je fais en vos jours une œuvre \q que vous ne croiriez pas si on vous la racontait.
fr.R: Regardez ce qui se passe parmi les nations ! \q Soyez étonnés et stupéfaits ! \q Je vais faire de votre vivant quelque chose \q que vous ne croiriez pas, même si on vous le racontait.

sw.L: Tazameni kati ya mataifa, mkaangalie, \q mkastaajabu, mshangae! \q Kwa maana ninafanya kazi katika siku zenu \q [ambayo] hamngeiamini kama ingesimuliwa.
sw.B: Yatazameni mataifa, mkaangalie, \q mkastaajabu kabisa! \q Kwa maana ninafanya kazi katika siku zenu \q ambayo hamngeiamini hata kama mngeambiwa.
sw.R: Tazameni yanayotokea kati ya mataifa! \q Shangaeni na kustaajabu! \q Nitafanya jambo wakati wa maisha yenu \q ambalo hamngeliamini hata kama mtu angewaambia.

vi.L: Hãy nhìn giữa các dân tộc, và hãy xem, \q hãy kinh ngạc, hãy sửng sốt! \q Vì [{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}] làm một việc trong đời các ngươi, \q [một việc] các ngươi sẽ không tin nếu được kể lại.
vi.B: Hãy nhìn các dân tộc và quan sát, \q hãy hết sức kinh ngạc! \q Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang làm một việc trong đời các ngươi \q mà dù có người kể lại, các ngươi cũng không tin.
vi.R: Hãy nhìn những gì đang xảy ra giữa các dân tộc! \q Hãy kinh ngạc và sửng sốt! \q Ta sắp làm một việc ngay trong đời các ngươi \q mà dù có ai kể lại, các ngươi cũng không tin.

ko.L: 너희는 민족들 가운데를 보고 살펴보아라. \q 놀라고 또 놀라라. \q 너희 시대에 [내가] 한 가지 일을 행하고 있으니, \q 그것을 전해 들어도 너희가 믿지 못할 것이다.
ko.B: 민족들을 보고 살펴보아라. \q 몹시 놀라라. \q 내가 너희 시대에 한 가지 일을 하고 있으니, \q 누가 너희에게 말해 주어도 너희가 믿지 못할 일이다.
ko.R: 민족들 가운데서 일어나는 일을 보아라. \q 깜짝 놀라고 어리둥절해하여라. \q 너희가 살아 있는 동안에 내가 한 가지 일을 하려고 한다. \q 누가 너희에게 말해 주어도 너희는 믿지 못할 것이다.

decisions.choice: the LORD answers: "I am doing a work"
decisions.reason: The speaker changes: the LORD answers Habakkuk's complaint. "You" is plural, Habakkuk and his people. The Hebrew says "doing a work" without naming who does it; verse 6 shows that it is the LORD ("I am raising up").

decisions.choice: be astonished, be astounded: the same verb twice, for emphasis
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated in two forms, a Hebrew way of saying "be utterly amazed". The shock is that God will answer the injustice in Judah by bringing the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: Acts 13:41 quotes this verse in its Greek form
decisions.reason: At the end of his sermon in Pisidian Antioch, Paul warns his hearers with this verse: "Look, you scoffers, and wonder, and perish, for I am working a work in your days" (Acts 13:41). He quotes the Greek translation, which has "you scoffers" where the Hebrew has "among the nations" (the Hebrew words are close in form) and adds "perish". As in Habakkuk, the warning is that God is doing something that his hearers would not believe.

decisions.choice: [I am] (L); I am (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves out the subject of "working"; Literal brackets "I am", and Balanced and Readable write it, following verse 6 (m1).

decisions.choice: The plural "you" (Habakkuk and his people) takes plural_you spans, verbs included: "{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} entre las naciones", "{{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} días"
decisions.reason: The LORD answers a group (m1); every plural "you" in the book takes the ustedes / vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: "hago una obra en sus días" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Acts 13:41 quotes this verse (m3); Spanish keeps its words "hago una obra en sus días" so that the quotation can be seen, though Acts follows the Greek elsewhere ("despreciadores").

decisions.choice: "une œuvre en vos jours" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Acts 13:41 quotes this verse; French keeps the published Acts' key words "une œuvre en vos jours" where the Hebrew means the same, without Acts' Greek-only wording ("vous qui méprisez").

decisions.choice: "ninafanya kazi katika siku zenu" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The words of Acts 13:41, which quotes this verse from the Greek (m3); "ninafanya" carries the subject in the verb, so nothing is bracketed.

decisions.choice: "làm một việc trong đời các ngươi"; God says "các ngươi" to Habakkuk and his people
decisions.reason: The wording of Acts 13:41, which quotes this verse (m3); the plural "you" is the oracle's "các ngươi".

decisions.choice: "너희 시대에 … 한 가지 일을" (L, B); "놀라고 또 놀라라" (L) for the doubled verb
decisions.reason: The words of Acts 13:41, which quotes this verse (m3); God speaks 해라체 to the people as 너희.

source.text: כִּֽי־הִנְנִ֤י מֵקִים֙ אֶת־הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים הַגּ֖וֹי הַמַּ֣ר וְהַנִּמְהָ֑ר הַֽהוֹלֵךְ֙ לְמֶרְחֲבֵי־אֶ֔רֶץ לָרֶ֖שֶׁת מִשְׁכָּנ֥וֹת לֹּא־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For look, I [am] raising up the Chaldeans, the nation the bitter and the impetuous, the [one] going to [the] breadths of [the] earth to possess dwellings not to it.

en.L: For look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, \q that bitter and impetuous nation, \q who march through the breadth of the earth \q to take possession of dwellings [that are] not theirs.
en.B: For I am raising up the Chaldeans, \q that fierce and reckless nation, \q who sweep across the wide earth \q to seize homes that are not their own.
en.R: I am bringing the Babylonians to power. \q They are cruel and quick to attack. \q They march across the whole earth \q to take over homes that belong to other people.

es.L: Porque he aquí, yo levanto a los caldeos, \q esa nación amarga e impetuosa, \q que marcha por las anchuras de la tierra \q para poseer moradas [que] no [son] suyas.
es.B: Porque yo levanto a los caldeos, \q esa nación feroz e impetuosa, \q que recorre la tierra a lo ancho \q para apoderarse de moradas que no le pertenecen.
es.R: Voy a darles el poder a los babilonios. \q Son crueles y rápidos para atacar. \q Marchan por toda la tierra \q para quedarse con las casas de otros.

fr.L: Car voici, je fais lever les Chaldéens, \q cette nation amère et impétueuse, \q qui marche à travers les étendues de la terre \q pour s’emparer de demeures [qui ne sont] pas à elle.
fr.B: Car je suscite les Chaldéens, \q cette nation féroce et fougueuse, \q qui parcourt la terre dans toute son étendue \q pour s’emparer de demeures qui ne lui appartiennent pas.
fr.R: Je vais donner le pouvoir aux Babyloniens. \q Ils sont cruels et prompts à attaquer. \q Ils traversent toute la terre \q pour prendre les maisons des autres.

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, ninawainua Wakaldayo, \q taifa lile chungu na la pupa, \q linalopita katika upana wa dunia \q kumiliki makao yasiyo yake.
sw.B: Kwa maana ninawainua Wakaldayo, \q taifa lile katili na la haraka, \q linalopita katika dunia yote kwa upana wake \q kunyakua makao yasiyo yao.
sw.R: Ninawapa Wababeli mamlaka. \q Wao ni wakatili na wepesi kushambulia. \q Wanapita katika dunia yote \q kunyakua nyumba za watu wengine.

vi.L: Vì này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} dấy lên người Canh-đê, \q dân tộc cay nghiệt và hung hăng ấy, \q đi khắp bề rộng của đất \q để chiếm lấy những chỗ ở không [thuộc về] nó.
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} dấy lên người Canh-đê, \q dân tộc hung bạo và hấp tấp ấy, \q tràn qua khắp mặt đất bao la \q để chiếm đoạt nhà cửa không thuộc về chúng.
vi.R: Ta đang trao quyền lực cho người Ba-by-lôn. \q Chúng hung ác và nhanh chóng tấn công. \q Chúng tiến quân khắp mặt đất \q để chiếm nhà cửa của người khác.

ko.L: 보아라, 내가 갈대아 사람들을 일으킨다. \q 그들은 사납고 성급한 민족이니, \q 땅의 넓은 곳을 두루 다니며 \q 자기 것이 아닌 거처들을 차지할 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 갈대아 사람들을 일으킨다. \q 그들은 사납고 거침없는 민족이다. \q 그들은 넓은 땅을 휩쓸고 다니며 \q 남의 집들을 빼앗을 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 바빌로니아 사람들이 힘을 얻게 하겠다. \q 그들은 잔인하고 재빨리 공격한다. \q 그들은 온 땅을 누비며 \q 다른 사람들의 집을 차지할 것이다.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans were a people of southern Babylonia. A Chaldean dynasty took power in Babylon in 626 BC under Nabopolassar, helped to destroy Nineveh in 612 BC, and under Nebuchadnezzar defeated Egypt at Carchemish in 605 BC. Babylon then ruled Judah, took Jerusalem in 597 BC and destroyed it in 587/586 BC.

decisions.choice: I am raising up: God uses a pagan nation as his instrument
decisions.reason: The LORD says that it is he who raises up the Babylonians, as he called Assyria "the rod of my anger" (Isaiah 10:5) and Nebuchadnezzar "my servant" (Jeremiah 25:9). This answer troubles Habakkuk even more, and leads to his second complaint (1:12-17): how can a holy God use a nation more wicked than those it punishes?

decisions.choice: bitter and impetuous: savage and swift
decisions.reason: "Bitter" means fierce and cruel, like a bear robbed of its cubs (2 Samuel 17:8; Judges 18:25). "Impetuous" is hasty, rushing ahead without restraint.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and Jeremiah, Literal and Balanced say "Chaldeans" and Readable says "Babylonians". Readable says "bringing ... to power" for "raising up".

decisions.choice: "los caldeos" (L, B); "los babilonios" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled names, as 2 Kings 25 and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: "les Chaldéens" (L, B); "les Babyloniens" (R)
decisions.reason: As the French prophets and 2 Kings 25: the people's own name at Literal and Balanced, the name a new reader knows at Readable, as the English.

decisions.choice: "Wakaldayo" (L, B); "Wababeli" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled names, as 2 Chronicles 36:17 and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: "người Canh-đê" (L, B); "người Ba-by-lôn" (R); "chúng" for the invaders
decisions.reason: The settled names (2 Kings 25); the oracle calls the enemy nation "chúng", as the prophets do.

decisions.choice: "갈대아 사람들" (L, B); "바빌로니아 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled names, as 2 Kings 25:4 and Jeremiah.

source.text: אָיֹ֥ם וְנוֹרָ֖א ה֑וּא מִמֶּ֕נּוּ מִשְׁפָּט֥וֹ וּשְׂאֵת֖וֹ יֵצֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Terrifying and fearsome [is] it; from itself its justice and its dignity go forth.

en.L: Dreadful and fearsome [is] it; \q from itself its justice and its dignity go forth.
en.B: They are feared and dreaded; \q they set their own law and claim their own honor.
en.R: People are terrified of them. \q They make their own rules and answer to no one.

es.L: Terrible y temible [es] ella; \q de sí misma salen su derecho y su dignidad.
es.B: Son temidos y espantosos; \q ellos mismos fijan su ley y reclaman su propia honra.
es.R: La gente les tiene terror. \q Hacen sus propias reglas y no rinden cuentas a nadie.

fr.L: Terrible et redoutable [est]-elle ; \q d’elle-même sortent son droit et sa dignité.
fr.B: Ils sont craints et redoutés ; \q ils fixent eux-mêmes leur loi et réclament leur propre honneur.
fr.R: Tout le monde a terriblement peur d’eux. \q Ils font leurs propres règles et ne rendent de comptes à personne.

sw.L: Ni la kutisha na la kuogofya; \q hukumu yake na heshima yake hutoka kwake lenyewe.
sw.B: Wanaogopwa na kutisha; \q wanajiwekea sheria yao wenyewe na kujidai heshima yao wenyewe.
sw.R: Watu wanawaogopa sana. \q Wanajitungia sheria zao wenyewe, wala hawawajibiki kwa mtu yeyote.

vi.L: Nó đáng khiếp và đáng sợ; \q công lý và uy quyền của nó phát xuất từ chính nó.
vi.B: Chúng thật đáng sợ và khủng khiếp; \q chúng tự đặt luật lệ cho mình và tự đề cao danh dự của mình.
vi.R: Ai cũng khiếp sợ chúng. \q Chúng tự đặt luật lệ và chẳng phải chịu trách nhiệm với ai.

ko.L: 그 민족은 무섭고 두렵다. \q 그 정의와 위엄이 그 자신에게서 나온다.
ko.B: 그들은 무섭고 두려운 자들이다. \q 그들은 스스로 법을 정하고 스스로 영예를 내세운다.
ko.R: 사람들은 그들을 몹시 두려워한다. \q 그들은 제멋대로 규칙을 만들고 아무에게도 책임지지 않는다.

decisions.choice: from itself its justice and its dignity go forth: it answers to no one
decisions.reason: The nation decides for itself what is right and claims its own greatness; it recognizes no law above its own will. The word "justice" picks up verse 4: Judah's justice is twisted, and the justice of the Babylonians is whatever they decide.

decisions.choice: they (B, R) for "it"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the nation as "it" (or "he"). Balanced and Readable say "they", the Babylonians, which reads more naturally in English and does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: "ella" (L), agreeing with "nación"; "ellos" (B, R), the Chaldeans
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "it" is the nation of verse 6; Balanced and Readable say "they", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "elle" (L), agreeing with "nation"; "ils" (B, R), the Chaldeans
alternatives: "il" at L, as the Hebrew masculine
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the nation as "it"; French "nation" is feminine, so Literal says "elle" through verse 11, and Balanced and Readable say "ils", as the English "they".

decisions.choice: "그 민족은" (L) for the Hebrew "it"
decisions.reason: Korean has no natural neuter pronoun for a nation; Literal names the nation of verse 6, and Balanced and Readable say "그들".

source.text: וְקַלּ֨וּ מִנְּמֵרִ֜ים סוּסָ֗יו וְחַדּוּ֙ מִזְּאֵ֣בֵי עֶ֔רֶב וּפָ֖שׁוּ פָּֽרָשָׁ֑יו וּפָֽרָשָׁיו֙ מֵרָח֣וֹק יָבֹ֔אוּ יָעֻ֕פוּ כְּנֶ֖שֶׁר חָ֥שׁ לֶאֱכֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: And swifter than leopards [are] its horses, and fiercer than wolves of [the] evening; and its horsemen gallop, and its horsemen from afar come; they fly like an eagle hastening to devour.

en.L: Swifter than leopards [are] its horses, and fiercer than wolves of [the] evening; \q and its horsemen gallop proudly; \q and its horsemen come from afar; \q they fly like an eagle hurrying to devour.
en.B: Their horses are swifter than leopards, \q fiercer than wolves at dusk. \q Their horsemen charge ahead; \q their riders come from far away; \q they swoop like an eagle rushing to devour.
en.R: Their horses are faster than leopards \q and fiercer than hungry wolves at sunset. \q Their soldiers on horseback charge ahead. \q They come from far away. \q They swoop down like eagles rushing to catch their food.

es.L: Más veloces que leopardos [son] sus caballos, y más feroces que lobos de [la] tarde; \q y sus jinetes galopan con arrogancia; \q y sus jinetes vienen de lejos; \q vuelan como águila que se apresura a devorar.
es.B: Sus caballos son más veloces que leopardos, \q más feroces que lobos al anochecer. \q Sus jinetes se lanzan al ataque; \q sus jinetes vienen de lejos; \q se abalanzan como águila que se precipita a devorar.
es.R: Sus caballos son más rápidos que los leopardos \q y más feroces que los lobos hambrientos al caer la tarde. \q Sus soldados a caballo atacan. \q Vienen desde muy lejos. \q Se lanzan como águilas que bajan a toda prisa a atrapar su comida.

fr.L: Plus rapides que des léopards [sont] ses chevaux, et plus féroces que des loups du soir ; \q et ses cavaliers galopent fièrement ; \q et ses cavaliers viennent de loin ; \q ils volent comme un aigle qui se hâte de dévorer.
fr.B: Leurs chevaux sont plus rapides que des léopards, \q plus féroces que des loups au crépuscule. \q Leurs cavaliers chargent ; \q leurs cavaliers viennent de loin ; \q ils fondent comme l’aigle qui se précipite pour dévorer.
fr.R: Leurs chevaux sont plus rapides que des léopards \q et plus féroces que des loups affamés à la tombée de la nuit. \q Leurs soldats à cheval foncent en avant. \q Ils viennent de loin. \q Ils fondent sur leur proie comme des aigles qui se précipitent pour attraper leur nourriture.

sw.L: Farasi wake [ni] wepesi kuliko chui, na wakali kuliko mbwa-mwitu wa jioni; \q na wapanda farasi wake wanapiga mbio kwa kiburi; \q na wapanda farasi wake wanakuja kutoka mbali; \q wanapaa kama tai anayeharakisha kula.
sw.B: Farasi wao ni wepesi kuliko chui, \q wakali kuliko mbwa-mwitu wakati wa machweo. \q Wapanda farasi wao wanashambulia mbele; \q wapanda farasi wao wanakuja kutoka mbali; \q wanashuka kama tai anayeharakisha kula.
sw.R: Farasi wao ni wepesi kuliko chui \q na wakali kuliko mbwa-mwitu wenye njaa wakati wa jioni. \q Askari wao wapanda farasi wanashambulia. \q Wanakuja kutoka mbali. \q Wanashuka kama tai wanaoharakisha kukamata chakula chao.

vi.L: Ngựa của nó nhanh hơn beo, và dữ tợn hơn sói [lúc] chiều tối; \q và kỵ binh của nó phi ngựa hiên ngang; \q và kỵ binh của nó từ xa đến; \q chúng bay như đại bàng vội vã đến ăn nuốt.
vi.B: Ngựa của chúng nhanh hơn beo, \q dữ tợn hơn sói lúc chập tối. \q Kỵ binh của chúng xông tới; \q kỵ binh của chúng từ xa kéo đến; \q chúng lao xuống như đại bàng vội vã vồ mồi.
vi.R: Ngựa của chúng chạy nhanh hơn beo \q và dữ hơn bầy sói đói lúc hoàng hôn. \q Quân kỵ mã của chúng xông lên phía trước. \q Chúng đến từ nơi xa. \q Chúng lao xuống như đại bàng sà xuống bắt mồi.

ko.L: 그 말들은 표범보다 빠르고, 저녁 이리보다 사나우며, \q 그 기병들은 거만하게 내달리고, \q 그 기병들은 먼 곳에서 오며, \q 먹이를 삼키려고 서두르는 독수리처럼 날아온다.
ko.B: 그들의 말은 표범보다 빠르고 \q 해 질 녘의 이리보다 사납다. \q 그들의 기병들은 앞으로 내달리고, \q 그들의 기병들이 먼 데서 온다. \q 먹이를 덮치려고 달려드는 독수리처럼 날아든다.
ko.R: 그들의 말은 표범보다 빠르고 \q 해 질 무렵 굶주린 이리보다 사납다. \q 말 탄 군사들이 앞으로 돌진한다. \q 그들은 멀리서 온다. \q 먹이를 잡으려고 내리꽂는 독수리처럼 덮친다.

decisions.choice: wolves of the evening: hungry wolves hunting at dusk
decisions.reason: Wolves hunt at nightfall after a day without food (Zephaniah 3:3; Jeremiah 5:6). The leopard, the wolf and the eagle are the swiftest and fiercest hunters the hearers knew.

decisions.choice: its horsemen gallop proudly
decisions.reason: The verb is rare and its sense is uncertain: it may mean to gallop, to paw the ground, or to spread out. The word for horsemen is repeated in the next line; the first may mean "horses" or "chargers".

decisions.choice: an eagle: a great bird of prey
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers the eagle and the vulture. It is the bird that swoops on its prey from a great height (Deuteronomy 28:49; Jeremiah 48:40).

decisions.choice: Their horses (B, R); charge ahead (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "their" for "its" (see verse 7). "Charge ahead" gives the sense of the uncertain verb (m2). Readable adds "hungry" (m1) and "to catch their food".

source.text: כֻּלֹּה֙ לְחָמָ֣ס יָב֔וֹא מְגַמַּ֥ת פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם קָדִ֑ימָה וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף כַּח֖וֹל שֶֽׁבִי׃

records.literal_gloss: All of it for violence comes; the totality of their faces [is] forward; and it gathers like sand captives.

en.L: All of it comes for violence; \q the mass of their faces [is set] forward; \q and it gathers captives like sand.
en.B: They all come intent on violence; \q their faces are set straight ahead, \q and they gather captives like sand.
en.R: They all come to do violence. \q Their army keeps pressing forward, \q and they take more prisoners than anyone can count.

es.L: Toda ella viene para la violencia; \q el conjunto de sus rostros [está vuelto] hacia adelante; \q y recoge cautivos como arena.
es.B: Todos vienen resueltos a la violencia; \q sus rostros miran fijamente adelante, \q y recogen cautivos como arena.
es.R: Todos vienen a hacer violencia. \q Su ejército sigue avanzando, \q y toman más prisioneros de los que se pueden contar.

fr.L: Tout entière elle vient pour la violence ; \q l’ensemble de leurs visages [est tourné] en avant ; \q et elle amasse des captifs comme du sable.
fr.B: Ils viennent tous, avides de violence ; \q leurs visages sont tournés droit devant, \q et ils ramassent des captifs comme du sable.
fr.R: Ils viennent tous pour commettre des violences. \q Leur armée avance sans cesse, \q et ils font plus de prisonniers qu’on ne peut en compter.

sw.L: Lote linakuja kwa ajili ya ukatili; \q wingi wa nyuso zao [umeelekea] mbele; \q nalo linakusanya mateka kama mchanga.
sw.B: Wote wanakuja wakiwa na nia ya ukatili; \q nyuso zao zimeelekezwa mbele moja kwa moja, \q nao wanakusanya mateka kama mchanga.
sw.R: Wote wanakuja kufanya ukatili. \q Jeshi lao linaendelea kusonga mbele, \q nao wanachukua mateka wengi kuliko mtu anavyoweza kuhesabu.

vi.L: Tất cả nó đến vì bạo lực; \q toàn thể mặt chúng [hướng] về phía trước; \q và nó gom phu tù như cát.
vi.B: Tất cả chúng kéo đến để làm điều bạo ngược; \q mặt chúng hướng thẳng về phía trước, \q và chúng gom phu tù như cát.
vi.R: Tất cả chúng đến để gây bạo lực. \q Đạo quân của chúng cứ tiến tới, \q và chúng bắt tù binh nhiều không đếm xuể.

ko.L: 그 민족이 모두 폭력을 위해 오고, \q 그들의 얼굴을 모두 앞으로 [향하며], \q 모래처럼 포로를 모은다.
ko.B: 그들은 모두 폭력을 휘두르려고 온다. \q 그들은 얼굴을 곧장 앞으로 향하고, \q 모래알처럼 많은 포로를 사로잡는다.
ko.R: 그들은 모두 폭력을 휘두르러 온다. \q 그들의 군대는 계속 밀고 나아가고, \q 셀 수 없이 많은 사람을 포로로 잡아간다.

decisions.choice: the mass of their faces [is set] forward: a very uncertain line
alternatives: their faces are like the east wind
decisions.reason: The first word is used only here and its meaning is not known; it may mean "the whole", "the throng" or "the eagerness". The last word means "eastward" or "forward"; with a small change it is "the east wind", the scorching wind from the desert (Jeremiah 18:17). The line may say that the whole army faces forward, or that their faces are like the east wind. Either way the army advances without turning aside.

decisions.choice: captives like sand: countless captives
decisions.reason: Sand is the common picture of a number too great to count (Genesis 22:17; Judges 7:12).

decisions.choice: They all (B, R); their faces are set straight ahead (B); keeps pressing forward (R); more prisoners than anyone can count (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the reading in m1 and say "they" for "it". Readable explains "like sand".

source.text: וְהוּא֙ בַּמְּלָכִ֣ים יִתְקַלָּ֔ס וְרֹזְנִ֖ים מִשְׂחָ֣ק ל֑וֹ ה֚וּא לְכָל־מִבְצָ֣ר יִשְׂחָ֔ק וַיִּצְבֹּ֥ר עָפָ֖ר וַֽיִּלְכְּדָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it at kings scoffs, and rulers [are] a laughingstock to it; it at every fortress laughs, and it heaps up earth and captures it.

en.L: And it scoffs at kings, \q and rulers [are] a joke to it; \q it laughs at every fortress, \q and heaps up earth and captures it.
en.B: They scoff at kings \q and make fun of rulers; \q they laugh at every fortress, \q for they pile up earth and take it.
en.R: They make fun of kings \q and laugh at rulers. \q They laugh at every fort, \q because they build ramps of earth and capture it.

es.L: Y ella se burla de los reyes, \q y los gobernantes [son] para ella cosa de risa; \q ella se ríe de toda fortaleza, \q y amontona tierra y la toma.
es.B: Se burlan de los reyes \q y se mofan de los gobernantes; \q se ríen de toda fortaleza, \q pues amontonan tierra y la toman.
es.R: Se burlan de los reyes \q y se ríen de los gobernantes. \q Se ríen de todas las fortalezas, \q porque levantan rampas de tierra y las toman.

fr.L: Et elle se moque des rois, \q et les dignitaires [sont] un jeu pour elle ; \q elle rit de toute forteresse, \q et elle entasse de la terre et la prend.
fr.B: Ils se moquent des rois \q et tournent les princes en dérision ; \q ils rient de toute forteresse, \q car ils entassent de la terre et la prennent.
fr.R: Ils se moquent des rois \q et rient des dirigeants. \q Ils rient de toutes les forteresses, \q parce qu’ils construisent des rampes de terre et s’en emparent.

sw.L: Nalo huwadhihaki wafalme, \q na watawala [ni] kichekesho kwake; \q huicheka kila ngome, \q nalo hurundika udongo na kuiteka.
sw.B: Wanawadhihaki wafalme \q na kuwafanyia mzaha watawala; \q wanaicheka kila ngome, \q kwa kuwa wanarundika udongo na kuiteka.
sw.R: Wanawadhihaki wafalme \q na kuwacheka watawala. \q Wanaicheka kila ngome, \q kwa sababu wanajenga vilima vya udongo na kuiteka.

vi.L: Và nó chế nhạo các vua, \q và các quan cai trị [là] trò cười cho nó; \q nó cười nhạo mọi đồn lũy, \q và đắp đất lên mà chiếm lấy.
vi.B: Chúng chế giễu các vua \q và nhạo báng các nhà cầm quyền; \q chúng cười nhạo mọi đồn lũy, \q vì chúng đắp ụ đất mà chiếm lấy.
vi.R: Chúng chế giễu các vua \q và cười nhạo những người cầm quyền. \q Chúng cười nhạo mọi đồn lũy, \q vì chúng đắp dốc đất để leo lên chiếm lấy.

ko.L: 그 민족은 왕들을 비웃고, \q 통치자들은 그들에게 웃음거리[이다]. \q 그들은 모든 요새를 비웃으며, \q 흙을 쌓아 그것을 점령한다.
ko.B: 그들은 왕들을 조롱하고 \q 통치자들을 비웃는다. \q 그들은 모든 요새를 우습게 여긴다. \q 흙을 쌓아 올려 그것을 점령하기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그들은 왕들을 놀리고 \q 통치자들을 비웃는다. \q 그들은 모든 성을 우습게 본다. \q 흙으로 비탈을 쌓아서 성을 점령하기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: heaps up earth: builds a siege ramp
decisions.reason: Attackers piled earth and rubble against a city wall to make a ramp up which soldiers and battering rams could advance (2 Samuel 20:15; 2 Kings 19:32; Jeremiah 32:24). No fortress could keep the Babylonians out.

decisions.choice: build ramps of earth
decisions.reason: Readable says what heaping up earth is for (m1).

source.text: אָ֣ז חָלַ֥ף ר֛וּחַ וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ר וְאָשֵׁ֑ם ז֥וּ כֹח֖וֹ לֵאלֹהֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Then sweeps on [the] wind and passes on, and he becomes guilty, this [one whose] strength [is] his god.

en.L: Then [it] sweeps on [like the] wind and passes through, and it becomes guilty, \q this one whose strength [is] its god.
en.B: Then they sweep past like the wind and go on, guilty men \q whose own strength is their god.
en.R: Then they rush on like the wind and keep going. \q They are guilty, because they worship their own strength.

es.L: Entonces pasa [como el] viento y sigue de largo, y se hace culpable, \q aquel cuya fuerza [es] su dios.
es.B: Luego pasan como el viento y siguen adelante, hombres culpables \q cuya propia fuerza es su dios.
es.R: Luego pasan veloces como el viento y siguen su camino. \q Son culpables, porque adoran su propia fuerza.

fr.L: Alors [elle] passe [comme le] vent et traverse, et elle se rend coupable, \q elle dont la force [est] son dieu.
fr.B: Puis ils passent comme le vent et poursuivent leur route, des hommes coupables \q dont la force est leur dieu.
fr.R: Puis ils filent comme le vent et continuent leur chemin. \q Ils sont coupables, car ils adorent leur propre force.

sw.L: Kisha linapita kasi [kama] upepo na kuvuka, nalo linakuwa na hatia, \q huyu ambaye nguvu yake [ni] mungu wake.
sw.B: Kisha wanapita kasi kama upepo na kuendelea, watu wenye hatia \q ambao nguvu yao wenyewe ndiyo mungu wao.
sw.R: Kisha wanakimbia kama upepo na kuendelea mbele. \q Wana hatia, kwa sababu wanaiabudu nguvu yao wenyewe.

vi.L: Bấy giờ [nó] lướt qua [như] gió và đi qua, và nó mắc tội, \q kẻ này lấy sức mạnh mình [làm] thần của mình.
vi.B: Rồi chúng lướt qua như cơn gió và tiến tới, là những kẻ có tội \q lấy sức mạnh của mình làm thần.
vi.R: Rồi chúng lao đi như gió và cứ thế tiến tới. \q Chúng có tội, vì chúng thờ lạy chính sức mạnh của mình.

ko.L: 그때에 [그 민족이] 바람[처럼] 휩쓸고 지나가니, 그가 죄를 짓는다. \q 자기 힘이 자기 신인 자다.
ko.B: 그러고는 바람처럼 휩쓸고 지나가는데, 그들은 \q 자기 힘을 신으로 삼는 죄인들이다.
ko.R: 그러고 나서 그들은 바람처럼 몰아쳐 계속 나아간다. \q 그들은 자기 힘을 섬기니 죄가 있다.

decisions.choice: then it sweeps on like the wind
alternatives: then the wind sweeps on and passes by
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be read "then the wind sweeps on and passes" or "then it sweeps on like the wind". The second reading, taken here, compares the army to a wind that sweeps through and is gone (Isaiah 21:1).

decisions.choice: and it becomes guilty
alternatives: and he makes his own strength his god (Qumran commentary)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "and he becomes guilty". The commentary on Habakkuk found among the Dead Sea Scrolls reads a different verb, "and he sets" (his strength as his god), and some follow it. The translation keeps the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: whose strength is his god: self-worship
decisions.reason: The Babylonians trust in and worship their own might. This is the charge on which their judgment will rest: the LORD has used them, but they owe their success to no god but their own power (Isaiah 10:13-15; Habakkuk 1:16; 2:4-5).

decisions.choice: guilty men whose own strength is their god (B); they worship their own strength (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "they" for the singular "it" or "he". Readable makes plain that treating one's strength as god means worshiping it.

source.text: הֲל֧וֹא אַתָּ֣ה מִקֶּ֗דֶם יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛י קְדֹשִׁ֖י לֹ֣א נָמ֑וּת יְהוָה֙ לְמִשְׁפָּ֣ט שַׂמְתּ֔וֹ וְצ֖וּר לְהוֹכִ֥יחַ יְסַדְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Are not you from antiquity, Yahweh my God, my Holy One? We will not die. Yahweh, for judgment you have appointed it, and Rock, to reprove you have established it.

en.L: Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not from of old, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, my Holy One? We will not die. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have appointed it for judgment; \q and, Rock, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have established it to reprove.
en.B: Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not from everlasting, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my God, my Holy One? We will not die. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have appointed them to execute judgment; \q Rock, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have set them in place to bring correction.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have existed from the very beginning. You are my God, my holy God. We will not die. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have chosen the Babylonians to carry out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgment. \q You are our Rock, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have sent them to correct us.

es.L: ¿No eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} desde la antigüedad, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios mío, Santo mío? No moriremos. \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} lo has designado para el juicio; \q y, Roca, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} lo has establecido para corregir.
es.B: ¿No eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} desde siempre, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, mi Dios, mi Santo? No moriremos. \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} los has designado para ejecutar el juicio; \q Roca, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} los has puesto ahí para corregir.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has existido desde el principio. Eres mi Dios, mi Dios santo. No moriremos. \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has escogido a los babilonios para llevar a cabo {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} juicio. \q Eres nuestra Roca, y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} los has enviado para corregirnos.

fr.L: N’es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas dès les temps anciens, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mon Dieu, mon Saint ? Nous ne mourrons pas. \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as établie pour le jugement ; \q et, Rocher, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as fondée pour corriger.
fr.B: N’es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas depuis toujours, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, mon Dieu, mon Saint ? Nous ne mourrons pas. \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as chargés d’exécuter le jugement ; \q Rocher, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as placés là pour corriger.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} existes depuis le tout début. Tu es mon Dieu, mon Dieu saint. Nous ne mourrons pas. \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as choisi les Babyloniens pour exécuter {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} jugement. \q Tu es notre Rocher, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as envoyés pour nous corriger.

sw.L: Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} si wa tangu zamani, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu, Mtakatifu wangu? Hatutakufa. \q Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, umeliweka kwa ajili ya hukumu; \q na, Ee Mwamba, umeliimarisha ili kuonya.
sw.B: Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} si wa tangu milele, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wangu, Mtakatifu wangu? Hatutakufa. \q Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, umewaweka watekeleze hukumu; \q Ee Mwamba, umewasimamisha ili walete marudi.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umekuwepo tangu mwanzo kabisa. Wewe ni Mungu wangu, Mungu wangu mtakatifu. Hatutakufa. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, umewachagua Wababeli watekeleze hukumu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. \q Wewe ni Mwamba wetu, {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} umewatuma ili watufundishe adabu.

vi.L: Chẳng phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [có] từ thuở xưa sao, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của con, Đấng Thánh của con? Chúng con sẽ không chết. \q Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lập nó để thi hành sự phán xét; \q và, lạy Vầng Đá, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đặt nó để quở trách.
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của con, Đấng Thánh của con, chẳng phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hằng có từ muôn đời sao? Chúng con sẽ không chết. \q Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lập chúng để thi hành sự phán xét; \q lạy Vầng Đá, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đặt chúng để sửa phạt.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã có từ ban đầu. Ngài là Đức Chúa Trời của con, Đức Chúa Trời thánh khiết của con. Chúng con sẽ không chết. \q Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chọn người Ba-by-lôn để thi hành sự phán xét của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Ngài là Vầng Đá của chúng con, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã sai chúng đến để sửa phạt chúng con.

ko.L: 주님은 옛적부터 [계신 분이] 아니십니까, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 나의 하나님, 나의 거룩하신 분이시여? 저희는 죽지 않을 것입니다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 심판하시려고 그를 세우셨고, \q 반석이시여, 꾸짖으시려고 그를 두셨습니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 나의 하나님, 나의 거룩하신 분이시여, 주님은 영원 전부터 계신 분이 아니십니까? 저희는 죽지 않을 것입니다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 심판을 집행하라고 그들을 세우셨습니다. \q 반석이시여, 주님께서 바로잡으시려고 그들을 그 자리에 두셨습니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님은 맨 처음부터 계셨습니다. 주님은 저의 하나님, 거룩하신 저의 하나님이십니다. 저희는 죽지 않을 것입니다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 바빌로니아 사람들을 택하셔서 주님의 심판을 이루게 하셨습니다. \q 주님은 저희의 반석이십니다. 주님께서 저희를 바로잡으시려고 그들을 보내셨습니다.

decisions.choice: the prophet's second complaint begins
decisions.reason: Habakkuk answers the LORD's words with a confession of faith and a new complaint. He begins with what he knows: the LORD is eternal, his own God and the Holy One. He ends with the question of verse 13: how can such a God use the Babylonians?

decisions.choice: We will not die
alternatives: You do not die (said of God, by scribal tradition)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "we will not die": the people trust that the eternal God will not let them be wiped out. Jewish scribal tradition lists this verse among a few places where the scribes are said to have changed the wording out of reverence, so that an original "You do not die", said of God, became "we will not die". The translation follows the text as it stands.

decisions.choice: appointed it for judgment ... to reprove: the Babylonians as the LORD's instrument
alternatives: to judge and correct the nations
decisions.reason: "It" is the Babylonian nation. The prophet accepts that the LORD has appointed it to judge and to correct, most likely Judah (verse 4), as the LORD said in verse 6. "Rock" is a title of God as the firm, safe refuge of his people (Deuteronomy 32:4; Psalm 18:3).

decisions.choice: them (B); the Babylonians, to correct us, our Rock (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "them" for the singular "it", the Babylonian nation; Readable names them and says whom they correct (m3). "Rock" keeps its capital as a title of God.

decisions.choice: "Roca", capitalized, as a title of God; the pronouns "lo" / "los" for the nation take no span
decisions.reason: As the Psalms (Psalm 18:3); only God's own pronouns are spanned, not the Babylonians'.

decisions.choice: "Ee Mwamba" (L, B), "Mwamba wetu" (R), capitalized as a title of God
decisions.reason: As the Psalms' "mwamba" for God as refuge (m3).

decisions.choice: "lạy Vầng Đá" (L, B), "Vầng Đá của chúng con" (R)
decisions.reason: "Vầng đá" is the Psalms' word for God as refuge, capitalized here as a title; "lạy" is the settled way of addressing God.

decisions.choice: "반석이시여" (L, B), "저희의 반석" (R); "나의 하나님, 나의 거룩하신 분"
decisions.reason: 반석 is the Psalms' word for God as the firm refuge (m3); the vocatives keep the Hebrew's "my".

source.text: טְה֤וֹר עֵינַ֨יִם֙ מֵרְא֣וֹת רָ֔ע וְהַבִּ֥יט אֶל־עָמָ֖ל לֹ֣א תוּכָ֑ל לָ֤מָּה תַבִּיט֙ בּֽוֹגְדִ֔ים תַּחֲרִ֕ישׁ בְּבַלַּ֥ע רָשָׁ֖ע צַדִּ֥יק מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [You are too] pure of eyes for seeing evil, and to look at trouble you are not able. Why do you look at [those who] act treacherously, [why] are you silent when swallows up a wicked [person] a righteous [person] more than him?

en.L: [You are too] pure of eyes to see evil, \q and to look on wrongdoing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are not able. \q Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} look on those who deal treacherously, \q [why] are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} silent when [the] wicked swallows up [one] more righteous than himself?
en.B: Your eyes are too pure to look on evil, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cannot look on wrongdoing. \q Why then do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} look on the treacherous, \q and keep silent while the wicked swallow up those more righteous than they?
en.R: Your eyes are so pure that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cannot stand to look at evil. \q You cannot put up with wrongdoing. \q So why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put up with these treacherous people? \q Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} silent while wicked people destroy those who are better than they are?

es.L: [Eres] demasiado puro de ojos para ver el mal, \q y mirar la iniquidad no puedes. \q ¿Por qué miras a los que actúan con traición, \q [por qué] callas cuando el malvado devora al [que es] más justo que él?
es.B: Tus ojos son demasiado puros para mirar el mal, \q y no puedes contemplar la iniquidad. \q ¿Por qué, entonces, miras a los traidores \q y callas mientras los malvados devoran a los que son más justos que ellos?
es.R: Tus ojos son tan puros que no soportas mirar el mal. \q No puedes tolerar lo que está mal. \q Entonces, ¿por qué toleras a esta gente traicionera? \q ¿Por qué callas mientras los malvados destruyen a los que son mejores que ellos?

fr.L: [Tu as les] yeux trop purs pour voir le mal, \q et regarder la peine, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne [le] peux pas. \q Pourquoi regardes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ceux qui agissent avec perfidie, \q [pourquoi] {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} tais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} quand le méchant engloutit [celui qui est] plus juste que lui ?
fr.B: Tes yeux sont trop purs pour voir le mal, \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne peux pas regarder l’injustice. \q Pourquoi donc regardes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les traîtres, \q et gardes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} le silence quand le méchant engloutit plus juste que lui ?
fr.R: Tes yeux sont si purs que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne supportes pas de voir le mal. \q Tu ne peux pas tolérer l’injustice. \q Alors pourquoi supportes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ces traîtres ? \q Pourquoi restes-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} silencieux quand des méchants détruisent des gens meilleurs qu’eux ?

sw.L: [Wewe ni] safi wa macho mno kuweza kuona uovu, \q na kutazama maovu huwezi. \q Kwa nini unawatazama wale wanaotenda kwa hila, \q [kwa nini] unanyamaza mwovu anapommeza [mtu] aliye mwenye haki kuliko yeye?
sw.B: Macho {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ni safi mno kutazama uovu, \q wala huwezi kuyatazama maovu. \q Basi kwa nini unawatazama wadanganyifu, \q na kunyamaza waovu wanapowameza walio na haki zaidi kuliko wao?
sw.R: Macho {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ni safi sana hata huwezi kuvumilia kutazama uovu. \q Huwezi kuvumilia maovu. \q Basi kwa nini unawavumilia watu hawa wadanganyifu? \q Kwa nini unanyamaza waovu wanapowaangamiza watu walio bora kuliko wao?

vi.L: [Ngài có] mắt quá tinh sạch để nhìn điều ác, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không thể nhìn xem điều gian tà. \q Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhìn xem những kẻ phản trắc, \q [sao] {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} im lặng khi kẻ ác nuốt [người] công chính hơn nó?
vi.B: Mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} quá tinh sạch, không thể nhìn điều ác, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không thể nhìn xem điều sai trái. \q Vậy sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại nhìn xem bọn phản trắc, \q và im lặng khi kẻ ác nuốt chửng những người công chính hơn chúng?
vi.R: Mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tinh sạch đến nỗi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không chịu nổi khi nhìn điều ác. \q Ngài không thể dung thứ điều sai trái. \q Vậy sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại dung thứ những kẻ phản trắc này? \q Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} im lặng trong khi kẻ ác tiêu diệt những người tốt hơn chúng?

ko.L: [주님은] 눈이 너무 정결하셔서 악을 보지 못하시며, \q 악행을 바라보실 수 없으십니다. \q 어찌하여 배신하는 자들을 바라보시며, \q 악인이 자기보다 의로운 [사람을] 삼킬 때 [어찌하여] 잠잠하십니까?
ko.B: 주님의 눈은 너무 정결하셔서 악을 보지 못하시고, \q 악행을 그냥 보아 넘기지 못하십니다. \q 그런데 어찌하여 배신자들을 보고만 계시며, \q 악인들이 자기들보다 의로운 사람들을 삼키는데도 잠잠하십니까?
ko.R: 주님의 눈은 너무나 깨끗하셔서 악한 것을 차마 보지 못하십니다. \q 주님은 나쁜 짓을 참지 못하십니다. \q 그런데 어찌하여 이 배신자들을 그냥 두십니까? \q 악한 사람들이 자기들보다 나은 사람들을 멸망시키는데 어찌하여 잠잠히 계십니까?

decisions.choice: too pure to look on evil, yet God seems to look on: Habakkuk's problem
decisions.reason: "Look on" means to tolerate or approve. Habakkuk sets what he believes about God's holiness beside what he sees: the LORD cannot approve evil, yet he lets the treacherous Babylonians prosper. The question is not answered until chapter 2.

decisions.choice: the treacherous: those who break faith
decisions.reason: The word is used of those who betray trust, break agreements and deal deceitfully (Isaiah 21:2; 24:16). Here it describes the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: the wicked swallows up one more righteous than himself
decisions.reason: The wicked is the Babylonian; the one "more righteous" is Judah, or the righteous within it. Habakkuk does not say that Judah is innocent (verses 2-4), only that it is not as wicked as the people sent to punish it.

decisions.choice: the wicked, those more righteous than they (B); wicked people, those who are better (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plurals for the Hebrew singulars, which stand for whole groups, so that no gender span is needed.

source.text: וַתַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֖ם כִּדְגֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם כְּרֶ֖מֶשׂ לֹא־מֹשֵׁ֥ל בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you have made humankind like the fish of the sea, like creeping things [that have] not a ruler over it.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made humankind like the fish of the sea, \q like creeping things [with] no ruler over them.
en.B: You have made people like fish in the sea, \q like creatures that crawl, with no ruler over them.
en.R: You have made people like fish in the sea, \q like little sea creatures that have no leader to protect them.

es.L: Y has hecho a la humanidad como los peces del mar, \q como los animales que se arrastran, [que] no [tienen] gobernante sobre ellos.
es.B: Has hecho a los seres humanos como peces del mar, \q como animales que se arrastran, sin nadie que los gobierne.
es.R: Has hecho a la gente como peces en el mar, \q como pequeñas criaturas marinas que no tienen un jefe que las proteja.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait l’humanité comme les poissons de la mer, \q comme les bêtes qui rampent, [qui n’ont] pas de maître sur elles.
fr.B: Tu as rendu les humains semblables aux poissons de la mer, \q aux bêtes qui rampent et n’ont pas de chef.
fr.R: Tu as rendu les gens pareils aux poissons de la mer, \q aux petites bêtes marines qui n’ont pas de chef pour les protéger.

sw.L: Nawe umewafanya wanadamu kama samaki wa baharini, \q kama viumbe vitambaavyo, visivyo na mtawala juu yao.
sw.B: Umewafanya watu kama samaki baharini, \q kama viumbe vitambaavyo, visivyo na mtawala.
sw.R: Umewafanya watu kama samaki baharini, \q kama viumbe vidogo vya baharini visivyo na kiongozi wa kuvilinda.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm cho loài người như cá biển, \q như loài bò sát không [có] kẻ cai trị trên chúng.
vi.B: Ngài đã khiến loài người như cá dưới biển, \q như loài bò sát không có ai cai trị.
vi.R: Ngài đã làm cho con người giống như cá dưới biển, \q như những sinh vật nhỏ dưới biển không có người lãnh đạo bảo vệ.

ko.L: 주님께서 사람을 바다의 물고기처럼, \q 다스리는 자가 없는 기어 다니는 것들처럼 만드셨습니다.
ko.B: 주님께서는 사람들을 바다의 물고기처럼, \q 다스리는 이 없는 기어 다니는 것들처럼 만드셨습니다.
ko.R: 주님께서는 사람들을 바다의 물고기처럼, \q 지켜 줄 우두머리가 없는 작은 바다 생물처럼 만드셨습니다.

decisions.choice: humankind like fish and creeping things: creation turned upside down
decisions.reason: In Genesis 1:26-28 humankind is made to rule over the fish of the sea and every creeping thing. Now, Habakkuk complains, God has let people be treated like fish themselves, with no ruler to protect them, as the next verses show.

decisions.choice: creeping things: small creatures that move about
decisions.reason: The word is used of small creatures on land and of the creatures of the sea (Psalm 104:25), which fits the fish of the first line.

decisions.choice: no leader to protect them
decisions.reason: Readable adds "to protect them" to say why having no ruler matters here.

source.text: כֻּלֹּה֙ בְּחַכָּ֣ה הֵֽעֲלָ֔ה יְגֹרֵ֣הוּ בְחֶרְמ֔וֹ וְיַאַסְפֵ֖הוּ בְּמִכְמַרְתּ֑וֹ עַל־כֵּ֖ן יִשְׂמַ֥ח וְיָגִֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: All of it with a hook he brings up; he drags it away in his net, and he gathers it in his dragnet; therefore he rejoices and is glad.

en.L: All of it he brings up with a hook; \q he drags it away in his net \q and gathers it in his dragnet; \q therefore he rejoices and is glad.
en.B: The enemy pulls them all up with a hook; \q he drags them away in his net \q and gathers them in his fishing net; \q so he rejoices and celebrates.
en.R: The Babylonians catch people with hooks. \q They drag them away in nets \q and gather them up in fishing nets. \q Then they celebrate and are happy.

es.L: A toda ella la saca con anzuelo; \q la arrastra en su red \q y la recoge en su red barredera; \q por eso se alegra y se regocija.
es.B: El enemigo los saca a todos con anzuelo; \q los arrastra en su red \q y los recoge en su red de pesca; \q por eso se alegra y hace fiesta.
es.R: Los babilonios atrapan a la gente con anzuelos. \q La arrastran en redes \q y la recogen en redes de pesca. \q Luego celebran y están felices.

fr.L: Tout entière il la fait monter à l’hameçon ; \q il la traîne dans son filet \q et la rassemble dans sa senne ; \q c’est pourquoi il se réjouit et exulte.
fr.B: L’ennemi les tire tous à l’hameçon ; \q il les entraîne dans son filet \q et les ramasse dans sa senne ; \q alors il se réjouit et jubile.
fr.R: Les Babyloniens attrapent les gens avec des hameçons. \q Ils les traînent dans des filets \q et les ramassent dans des filets de pêche. \q Puis ils font la fête, tout heureux.

sw.L: Wote huwavua kwa ndoano; \q huwakokota katika wavu wake \q na kuwakusanya katika juya lake; \q kwa hiyo anafurahi na kushangilia.
sw.B: Adui anawavua wote kwa ndoano; \q anawakokota katika wavu wake \q na kuwakusanya katika wavu wake wa kuvulia; \q kwa hiyo anafurahi na kusherehekea.
sw.R: Wababeli wanawavua watu kwa ndoano. \q Wanawakokota katika nyavu \q na kuwakusanya katika nyavu za kuvulia samaki. \q Kisha wanasherehekea na kufurahi.

vi.L: Nó dùng lưỡi câu kéo tất cả lên; \q nó lôi chúng đi trong lưới mình \q và gom chúng vào chài mình; \q vì vậy nó vui mừng và hớn hở.
vi.B: Kẻ thù dùng lưỡi câu kéo tất cả lên; \q nó lôi họ đi trong lưới mình \q và gom họ vào chài mình; \q vì thế nó vui mừng hớn hở.
vi.R: Người Ba-by-lôn bắt người ta bằng lưỡi câu. \q Chúng kéo họ đi trong lưới \q và gom họ vào chài. \q Rồi chúng ăn mừng và hớn hở.

ko.L: 그가 그 모두를 낚시로 끌어올리고, \q 자기 그물로 끌어가며, \q 자기 투망으로 모으니, \q 그러므로 그가 기뻐하고 즐거워합니다.
ko.B: 원수가 낚시로 그들을 모두 끌어올리고, \q 그물로 그들을 끌어가며, \q 고기 그물로 그들을 모아들이고는 \q 기뻐하며 즐거워합니다.
ko.R: 바빌로니아 사람들은 사람들을 낚싯바늘로 낚습니다. \q 그물로 그들을 끌고 가고 \q 고기 그물로 그들을 모아들입니다. \q 그러고는 신이 나서 기뻐합니다.

decisions.choice: hook and net: the conqueror catches people like fish
decisions.reason: The fisherman is the Babylonian, pictured as one person. The prophets use the hook and the net for conquest and captivity (Amos 4:2; Jeremiah 16:16; Ezekiel 29:4). Captives could be led away with hooks or ropes (2 Kings 19:28).

decisions.choice: net ... dragnet
decisions.reason: Two kinds of fishing net: the first is a casting net or seine, the second a dragnet pulled through the water. Together they catch everything.

decisions.choice: The enemy (B); The Babylonians (R); them (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "he" and "it". Balanced names him as "the enemy" and Readable as "the Babylonians", since the verse follows on from the Babylonians of verses 6-11 (m1), and both say "them" for the people caught.

decisions.choice: "A toda ella … la" (L), referring back to "la humanidad" of verse 14; "red barredera" (L) for the dragnet
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew's singular "it"; Balanced and Readable say "los" and "la gente", as the English "them".

decisions.choice: "Tout entière … la" (L), referring back to "l'humanité" of verse 14; "senne" (L, B) for the dragnet
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "all of it" points to humankind in verse 14, which French Literal calls "l'humanité", so the pronouns are feminine; the dragnet is a large drawn net, "senne", kept apart from the plain "filet".

decisions.choice: "juya" (L) for the dragnet, beside "wavu"
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew nets are different (m2); "juya" is the large seine drawn through the water.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet; for by them [is] rich his portion, and his food fat.

en.L: Therefore he sacrifices to his net \q and burns offerings to his dragnet, \q for by them his portion [is] rich \q and his food fat.
en.B: So he offers sacrifices to his net \q and burns incense to his fishing net, \q for by them he lives in plenty \q and eats the richest food.
en.R: So they offer sacrifices to their nets \q and burn incense to them, \q because their nets give them a life of luxury \q and the best food to eat.

es.L: Por eso ofrece sacrificios a su red \q y quema ofrendas a su red barredera, \q porque por ellas [es] pingüe su porción \q y suculenta su comida.
es.B: Por eso ofrece sacrificios a su red \q y quema incienso a su red de pesca, \q porque gracias a ellas vive en la abundancia \q y come los manjares más ricos.
es.R: Por eso ofrecen sacrificios a sus redes \q y les queman incienso, \q porque sus redes les dan una vida de lujo \q y la mejor comida.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi il sacrifie à son filet \q et brûle des offrandes à sa senne, \q car par eux sa part [est] grasse \q et sa nourriture riche.
fr.B: Alors il offre des sacrifices à son filet \q et brûle de l’encens à sa senne, \q car grâce à eux il vit dans l’abondance \q et mange les mets les plus riches.
fr.R: Alors ils offrent des sacrifices à leurs filets \q et brûlent de l’encens en leur honneur, \q parce que leurs filets leur donnent une vie de luxe \q et la meilleure nourriture.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo anatoa dhabihu kwa wavu wake \q na kufukiza kwa juya lake, \q kwa maana kwa sababu ya hivyo fungu lake [ni] nono \q na chakula chake kinono.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo anautolea wavu wake dhabihu \q na kulifukizia uvumba juya lake, \q kwa maana kwa hivyo anaishi kwa wingi \q na kula chakula kilicho bora.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo wanazitolea nyavu zao dhabihu \q na kuzifukizia uvumba, \q kwa sababu nyavu zao zinawapa maisha ya anasa \q na chakula kilicho bora kabisa.

vi.L: Vì vậy nó dâng tế lễ cho lưới mình \q và đốt lễ vật cho chài mình, \q vì nhờ chúng phần của nó [được] béo bở \q và thức ăn của nó béo ngậy.
vi.B: Vì thế nó dâng sinh tế cho lưới mình \q và đốt hương cho chài mình, \q vì nhờ chúng nó sống sung túc \q và ăn những món ngon nhất.
vi.R: Vì thế chúng dâng sinh tế cho lưới của chúng \q và đốt hương cho lưới, \q vì lưới đem lại cho chúng cuộc sống xa hoa \q và thức ăn ngon nhất.

ko.L: 그러므로 그가 자기 그물에 제사하고 \q 자기 투망에 제물을 살라 바칩니다. \q 그것들로 말미암아 그의 몫이 기름지고 \q 그의 음식이 풍성하기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그래서 그는 자기 그물에 제사를 드리고 \q 고기 그물에 향을 피웁니다. \q 그것들 덕분에 그가 풍족하게 살고 \q 가장 기름진 음식을 먹기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 그래서 그들은 자기 그물에 제물을 바치고 \q 그물 앞에 향을 피웁니다. \q 그 그물들이 그들에게 호화로운 생활과 \q 가장 좋은 음식을 주기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: he sacrifices to his net: he worships the means of his power
decisions.reason: The net stands for the army and weapons by which the Babylonian catches nations. To sacrifice to it is to give his own might the honor that belongs to God, as verse 11 says: "whose strength is his god".

decisions.choice: burns offerings, burns incense: makes offerings rise in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to send up in smoke, used of incense and of the fat of offerings. It is often used of worship given to other gods (Jeremiah 1:16; Hosea 11:2).

decisions.choice: he lives in plenty (B); a life of luxury (R)
decisions.reason: "His portion is rich and his food fat" means that he lives well; Balanced and Readable say so. Readable keeps the plural "they" of verse 15.

records.literal_gloss: Is he therefore to empty his net, and continually to kill nations not sparing?

en.L: Will he therefore empty his net, \q and continually kill nations without sparing?
en.B: Will he keep on emptying his net, \q killing nations without mercy, never stopping?
en.R: Will they keep emptying their nets to catch more? \q Will they never stop killing nations without mercy?

es.L: ¿Vaciará por eso su red, \q y matará continuamente naciones sin perdonar?
es.B: ¿Seguirá vaciando su red, \q matando naciones sin piedad, sin parar nunca?
es.R: ¿Seguirán vaciando sus redes para atrapar más? \q ¿Nunca dejarán de matar naciones sin piedad?

fr.L: Va-t-il donc vider son filet, \q et continuellement tuer des nations sans épargner ?
fr.B: Va-t-il continuer à vider son filet, \q à massacrer les nations sans pitié, sans jamais s’arrêter ?
fr.R: Vont-ils continuer à vider leurs filets pour en attraper encore plus ? \q Ne cesseront-ils jamais de tuer des nations sans pitié ?

sw.L: Je, kwa hiyo ataumwaga wavu wake, \q na kuua mataifa daima bila kuhurumia?
sw.B: Je, ataendelea kuumwaga wavu wake, \q akiua mataifa bila huruma, bila kukoma?
sw.R: Je, wataendelea kumwaga nyavu zao ili wakamate zaidi? \q Je, hawataacha kamwe kuua mataifa bila huruma?

vi.L: Có phải vì vậy mà nó cứ đổ lưới mình ra, \q và cứ giết các dân tộc không chút nương tay?
vi.B: Nó sẽ cứ trút lưới ra mãi sao, \q tàn sát các dân tộc không thương xót, chẳng bao giờ ngừng?
vi.R: Chúng sẽ cứ trút lưới ra để bắt thêm mãi sao? \q Chúng sẽ không bao giờ thôi giết các dân tộc không thương xót sao?

ko.L: 그러므로 그가 자기 그물을 비우고 \q 쉬지 않고 민족들을 무자비하게 죽여야 합니까?
ko.B: 그가 계속 자기 그물을 비우고 \q 끝도 없이 민족들을 사정없이 죽여도 됩니까?
ko.R: 그들이 더 잡으려고 언제까지 그물을 비우겠습니까? \q 언제까지 민족들을 무자비하게 죽이겠습니까?

decisions.choice: Will he therefore empty his net?: how long will this go on?
decisions.reason: The question ends the prophet's complaint: will the Babylonian keep emptying his net to fill it again, killing nations for ever? It is put to God, and the LORD answers in 2:2-20.

decisions.choice: empty his net
alternatives: empty his sword (draw it from its sheath; Qumran commentary)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "his net", continuing the fishing picture. The commentary on Habakkuk among the Dead Sea Scrolls reads "his sword", a word that differs by one letter. The meaning is close; the translation keeps the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: to catch more
decisions.reason: Readable says why the net is emptied: to be used again.
